questions.q: What is the verified result of checking row 2 and row 3 of the Steane code's H matrix for self-orthogonality?
options: Their entrywise product sums to 2, which is 0 mod 2, confirming orthogonality
Their entrywise product sums to 3, which is odd, so they are not orthogonal
Rows 2 and 3 are identical, so the check is meaningless
The check only applies to row 1, not rows 2 and 3
questions.explain: Row 2 and row 3 overlap in exactly 2 positions (columns 3 and 7), summing to 2, which is 0 mod 2 -- confirming the self-orthogonality the Steane code construction depends on.

questions.q: An X error hits qubit 3 of the Steane code. What is the resulting Z-type syndrome, and how is it computed?
options: (0,1,1) -- read column 3 of H, which has 0 in row 1 and 1 in rows 2 and 3
(1,1,1) -- every stabilizer always flips regardless of which qubit is hit
(0,0,0) -- X errors never produce a Z-type syndrome on the Steane code
questions.explain: Column 3 of H is [0,1,1], directly giving the Z-type syndrome (0,1,1) -- rows 2 and 3 flip because qubit 3 participates in those two stabilizers, row 1 doesn't.

questions.q: A Z error hits qubit 5 of the Steane code. What is the resulting X-type syndrome?
options: (1,0,1), read directly from column 5 of H
questions.explain: Column 5 of H is [1,0,1], giving X-type syndrome (1,0,1) -- rows 1 and 3 flip since qubit 5 participates in those stabilizers.

questions.q: Why does an X error on qubit 7 trigger all three Z-type stabilizers, syndrome (1,1,1)?
options: Because column 7 of H is [1,1,1] -- qubit 7 participates in every one of the 3 stabilizer rows
Because qubit 7 is not actually part of the Steane code
Because X errors always trigger every stabilizer regardless of which qubit is affected
Because row 3 of H has no 1s, forcing all other rows to compensate
questions.explain: Column 7 of H is [1,1,1], meaning qubit 7 is involved in all three parity checks, so an error there flips all three corresponding stabilizer outcomes.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call syndrome computation via 'reading a column of H' a practical payoff of the CSS construction specifically?
options: Because CSS stabilizers are built directly from a classical parity-check matrix, syndrome computation reduces to classical linear algebra instead of simulating the full quantum state
Because this shortcut only works for codes with fewer than 5 qubits
Because CSS codes don't actually have stabilizers, only classical parity checks
Because this method requires directly measuring the logical qubit's amplitudes
questions.explain: Since CSS stabilizers inherit their structure from a classical code's parity-check matrix, determining which stabilizers a given error triggers is a classical lookup -- a method that scales cleanly to much larger CSS codes like the surface code.
